claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain and toughness than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The WTaTiVZr alloy contains a chemically disordered matrix.
Chemical disorder in WTaTiVZr produces random lattice distortions.
Random lattice distortions promote activation of multiple or additional slip systems.
Random lattice distortions reduce dislocation pile-up.
Modified dislocation interactions enhance work hardening in WTaTiVZr.
Modified dislocation interactions delay crack propagation in WTaTiVZr.
Random lattice distortions lower and broaden the distribution of barriers to dislocation motion.
Enhanced work hardening and delayed crack initiation produce improved ductility and toughness under high-temperature loading.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have a higher strain-to-failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have higher fracture energy or toughness than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will display a more uniform distribution of activated slip systems than deformed tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will display a dislocation structure different from that of deformed tungsten.
Temperatures of approximately 1200–1500°C, inert atmosphere, and sustained mechanical loading are relevant to plasma-facing-component service.
The proposed comparison should use WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten specimens with similar grain sizes.
A failure to obtain at least a 20% increase in total plastic strain, together with no toughness enhancement and no evidence of modified dislocation dynamics, would falsify the hypothesis.
